entities.title: Report malformed JSON values as malformed-value
entities.summary: Where library-api §5 gives the shared code malformed-value, the TypeScript library reports codes of its own, so a caller matching on the shared code misses them.
entities.expected: JSON that isn't a well-formed value of the expected shape (wrong JSON types, missing or unexpected fields, a non-integer where an integer is required, a malformed rules bundle) is invalid with diagnostic code malformed-value, as docs/library-api.md §5 lists it. The C#, Java and Python libraries emit malformed-value.
entities.observed: The readers report type, missing-field, unexpected-field and unknown-component (internal.ts), resolve and toZone report invalid-rules for a malformed bundle (zones.ts), and fromEpochMilliseconds reports not-an-integer (native.ts). No source file emits malformed-value. The shared fixtures don't list malformed-value in expect.diagnostics, so they don't catch it.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of these failures includes the diagnostic code malformed-value (the existing code may stay alongside it).
A test asserts the code for a missing field, a wrong JSON type and a malformed rules bundle.

origin.description: readCivil, readRational and readAmount compared with docs/library-api.md §5, Diagnostic codes.

entities.title: Align TemporalContext.compare's diagnostics with the other libraries
entities.summary: TemporalContext.compare copies each side's resolve diagnostics, so two wall times in one overlap report ambiguous twice; C# and Java report one compare-level ambiguous warning.
entities.compromise: compare concatenates the diagnostics of both sides' resolve outcomes (info severity, one per ambiguous side), and the UTV-first example asserts ["ambiguous", "ambiguous"]. The Java library changed to a single compare-level ambiguous warning naming the possible orders, as the C# library does (implementations/java/CHANGELOG.md, Unreleased); the Python library still concatenates like this one.
entities.cost: The same comparison gives different diagnostics in different languages, and a Unique ordering can carry an ambiguous diagnostic from a side whose overlap did not change the order. docs/side-by-side.md shows the difference.
acceptanceCriteria: The five libraries report the same diagnostics from compare, as docs/library-api.md §4 is made to say.
test/examples/utv-first/temporal-context.test.ts asserts the agreed codes, and npm test passes.

origin.description: TemporalContext.compare, compared with implementations/csharp/src/Utv/Typed/ZonedValues.cs and the Java change of e0e80ff.

entities.title: Check the structural kind table against the schema
entities.summary: structural.ts holds each kind's required and allowed properties as a hand transcription of schema/utv-1.0.schema.json, and nothing compares the two.
entities.compromise: KINDS is "transcribed from schema/utv-1.0.schema.json" (its doc comment) rather than read from the schema file or checked against it. Only the shared valid and invalid examples exercise it.
entities.cost: A correction to the schema file, or a property the examples don't use, can leave the TypeScript validator accepting or rejecting what the schema does not, and no test would say so.
acceptanceCriteria: A test fails when KINDS and the schema's per-kind required and allowed properties differ, or KINDS is derived from the schema file.

entities.title: CivilDate.daysUntil throws beyond 2^53 days
entities.summary: daysUntil is a total operation on dates with bigint years, but returns a number, and throws an internal Error when the count does not fit one.
entities.expected: daysUntil(other) is total (docs/library-api.md §2, an integer) for any two dates the library can hold, since years are arbitrary precision (§1).
entities.observed: daysUntil calls the JSON layer's daysBetween through total(); for a count beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER daysBetween answers unsupported (implementation-limit) and total() throws Error("internal error: daysBetween gave unsupported (implementation-limit)").
acceptanceCriteria: daysUntil returns the exact count for any two CivilDates (for example as a bigint), or the API documents and tests the limit.

origin.description: CivilDate.daysUntil and total(), with ops.ts daysBetween's implementation-limit branch.
